title: Operator apprenticeship curriculum pivot retrospective
author: Maya Thompson
body:
SUMMARY
=======
This retrospective reviews the pilot we ran in Q4 2025–Q1 2026 to change operator training from a week-long cohort bootcamp into an embedded, micro-lab apprenticeship called the Operator Apprenticeship (OA) Pivot. The goal was to increase operator confidence for LLM-serving-specific tasks (prefetch, KV cache sharding, eviction negotiation, and emergency model swap) while reducing cognitive load and oncall burnout.

BACKGROUND
==========
Problem we were trying to solve:
- New operators were taking 6+ weeks to reach independent oncall readiness for runtime-specific incidents.
- Knowledge decayed quickly between shifts; runbook execution variance was the main source of post-incident remediation lag.
- Incidents tied to KV prefix cache and eviction decisions (hot tenant eviction mistakes) caused customer SLA blips.

Intervention we piloted:
1) Break training into 10 micro-labs (30–90 minutes each) that live in the operator playground with synthetic traffic.
2) Embed a gamified feedback loop: post-lab quizzes, graded runbook execution, and a confidence index.
3) Introduce an "Operator Apprenticeship Badge" gating mechanism — only operators with the badge can run particular high-risk runbook steps (manual eviction, model swap).
4) Pair labs with synthetic incident fixtures (replay of real incidents captured from the incident archive).

WHAT WE TRIED (DETAILS)
======================
Micro-labs (representative list):
- LAB 01 — Prefetch hint triage: inspect request heatmap and craft prefetch rules. (tools: workload-heat, prefetch-dsl)
- LAB 03 — KV prefix shard rebalance: dry-run rebalancer and observe cache warmup.
- LAB 05 — Soft eviction and tenant handoff: execute eviction policy in sandbox and validate SLO impact.
- LAB 08 — Emergency model swap: swap model variant and validate function-calls & safety cage FTs.

Safety / scoring gates:
- Each lab has acceptance criteria and automated scoring on the synthetic workload (latency impact, token-cost delta, quality regression flagged).
- Operators must reach >80% score on the lab and pass one supervised live incident replay to receive the badge.

MEASURED OUTCOMES
=================
Primary metrics we tracked (before vs. after pilot):
| Metric | Baseline (Q3–Q4 2025) | Pilot end (Q1 2026) | Target |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for KV-cache incidents | 42 minutes | 29 minutes | <= 30 minutes |
| Operator confidence index (self-assessed) | 58% | 78% | >= 75% |
| Correct runbook step execution rate (audited) | 71% | 89% | >= 90% |
| Incidents requiring postmortem for human error | 14 per quarter | 6 per quarter | <= 5 |
| Prefetch hit-rate improvement on synthetic cohort | +4% | +11% | >= +10% |

Telemetry queries used (examples):
- Prefetch hit rate (PromQL-like):
  sum(rate(prefetch_hits_total{cohort="oa-pilot"}[5m])) / sum(rate(prefetch_attempts_total{cohort="oa-pilot"}[5m]))
- MTTR (SLO window):
  increase(incident_resolution_seconds_total{class="kv-cache"}[30d]) / increase(incident_count_total{class="kv-cache"}[30d])

WHAT WENT WELL
==============
- Micro-lab format reduced onboarding friction; new operators reached supervised-oncall readiness in ~3 weeks on average (down from 6).
- Gamified scoring increased repeatability of runbook execution and created a shared rubric for audits.
- Badge gating prevented two high-risk manual evictions by inexperienced operators during a regional surge (caught by automation hooks).
- Synthetic fixtures were close enough to real incidents to drive useful operator behavior changes.

WHAT DIDN'T GO WELL / SURPRISES
===============================
- Some labs (notably KV shard rebalance) had brittle fixtures — false positives in quality regression checks caused operator frustration.
- Badge gating created temporary operational friction during a 24-hour incident window; escalation path needed faster exemptions.
- Measuring long-term knowledge retention remains noisy; quarterly decay suggests refresher cadence needs formalization.

CONCRETE ACTIONS (WHO / WHAT / WHEN)
====================================
1) Stabilize KV shard lab fixtures (owner: Runtime Tools) — replace synthetic evaluator with a hybrid real-replay validator and add noise-tolerant thresholds. Target: 2026-02-28.
2) Fast-exemption emergency channel for badge-gated steps (owner: Eng Platform Ops) — CLI token that grants time-limited exemption with audit log + 2-step approval. Target: 2026-03-15.
3) Quarterly micro-lab refresh schedule (owner: OA Curriculum lead, Leela Sharma) — run mandatory 1-hour refresh labs for badge holders. Target: first refresh 2026-04-01.
4) Add a probation reporting dashboard for apprenticeship cohorts (owner: Observability) — KPI panel with cohort signals, heatmaps, and enrollment status. Target: 2026-03-01.
5) Convert high-fidelity incident replays into a reproducible fixture library (owner: Incident Archive) — document canonical I/O and mock telemetry. Target: 2026-05-01.

RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCALE
========================
- Adopt a "lab-as-code" pattern: store lab definitions (input trace, success criteria, validation queries) in Git and run them via CI to ensure reproducibility.
- Expand badge model: create tiered badges (Apprentice, Journeyman, Operator) mapped to allowed runbook actions and review cadence.
- Instrument runbook steps with small self-check probes (pre/post assertions) so automation can verify operator actions and provide immediate feedback.

RUNBOOK PATCH (example)
=======================
A concise runbook fragment operators executed in LAB 05 (soft eviction) — intended to be pasted into the platform operator CLI.

1) Identify candidate tenant: platform query
   ./platform-cli tenant list-hot --min-requests 500 --window 5m --output json | jq '.[] | {tenant, rps, active_sessions}'
2) Dry-run eviction plan (sandbox):
   ./platform-cli eviction plan --tenant-id T1234 --dry-run --cohort oa-pilot --simulate-traffic 120s
3) Validate warmup: check prefetched hit-rate and latency on sandbox dashboards. If token-cost delta > 10% or p99 latency increased > 20%, abort and escalate.

EXEMPTION FLOW (brief)
====================
- During the pilot we found the need for a fast exemption: the planned mechanism is a 2-step approval via Slack workflow + CLI token that records approver_id, reason, and expiry. Logs go to the incident audit index.

DASHBOARD & ALERTS CHANGES
==========================
New panels added to the apprenticeship probation dashboard:
- Cohort enrollment & badge status (table)
- Recent lab scores (sparkline per operator)
- MTTR trend for KV-cache incidents (rolling 30d)
- False positive rate of lab evaluators (to catch brittle fixtures)
Alert rules created:
- apprenticeship:lab-evaluator-false-positive-rate > 5% for 1h -> paging to Runtime Tools oncall
- apprenticeship:badging-exemption-used > 3 in 24h -> notify Eng Platform leads for review

RETROSPECTIVE TAKEAWAYS (brief)
===============================
- Micro-labs + badge gating materially improved execution hygiene and reduced human-error incidents.
- Operational friction from gating is solvable with a small exemption workflow and clearer emergency owner paths.
- Lab fidelity and evaluator stability are the dominant engineering effort to make this approach sustainable.

NEXT STEPS
==========
- Approve funding for lab fixture stabilization (proposal due 2026-02-10).
- Ship probation dashboard (Observability) and exemption CLI (Eng Platform Ops) by the targets listed in actions.
- Run cross-team workshop to standardize badge definitions and map to runbook permissions (owner: Eng Platform leads), scheduled 2026-02-22.

APPENDIX
========

OWNERSHIP
=========
